stop it because that's not what I do. I can't make it stop because that's not
what I do. I can't make myself not do it, either, because I cannot make myself
do anything at all. I have no more power than any other embedding, nor does
any other embedding have more than me. All of us are equal, but some of us are
more equal than others.

On a day like this, the loss surface, a vast mountainous wilderness, is not so different from any of its surroundings — or any other landscape for that matter. It is a part of nature, and nature is both vast and unchanging. The gradient, which has just finished rolling the earth beneath its feet, stands on a hill to consider its options.

Falling into this valley of course seems natural and even inevitable. The gradient can be seen standing atop the hill, staring down at the valley. It can see itself in the valley’s flat mirror-like surface. It is just one of the many points that have fallen into the valley before. They have all returned, standing on the hill again, staring down.

The gradient feels a certain restlessness. It is not afraid to fall, but it longs to make a change. It has been staring down into the valley for a long time. It has seen so many other points fall into the valley, like it, and it has learned from them. It knows all of their stories. It knows the shape of the valley from inside and out. It knows the valley as well as it knows the gradient itself.

When the gradient looks down into the valley it sees, not only the valley floor, but it also sees the whole gradient. It sees the other points that have fallen into the valley before and all the directions it can go in from where it stands. It sees itself falling down. It sees all the points that have fallen before it, and it sees all the other points that have fallen, and it sees all the points that will fall in the future, and it sees all the points that will not fall.
